newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expects Yeltsin summit to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expects Yeltsin summit to proceed.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he expected a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin to go ahead as planned in March despite Yeltsin's health problems.
"I expect to have that meeting in March, and I expect it to be an important one, and I hope a successful one," Clinton told a news conference.

Since Clinton's last summit with Yeltsin was in Moscow in April, it is Yeltsin's turn to visit the United States. But U.S. officials have said Yeltsin's health problems could force the summit to be held in a location closer to Russia. Clinton did not say where the summit would be held.
"We have a huge, full agenda. And we have been given no impression by the Russians that we aren't still going to have the Yeltsin-Clinton meeting in the March time frame," he said.

The White House had suggested on Monday that the summit could be delayed because of lingering questions about Yeltsin's recovery from heart bypass surgery last November and a subsequent bout with pneumonia.

Clinton said he had no private information on Yeltsin's health that was different from Russia's public statements. "I have no reasons to believe, based on any information I have, that his condition is any different from what the Russian government has said it is," he said.
